newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq eases slightly in mixed session.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq eases slightly in mixed session.

text.p: Nasdaq shares eased slightly in a mixed session on Thursday, but small capitalization stocks showed modest gains, traders said.

Ending a three-day winning streak, the Nasdaq composite slipped 1.16 points or 0.08 percent to close unofficially at 1372.59. Advancing issues outpaced decliners 2159 to 2005 with a total of 563 million shares changing hands.

Although several large capitalization stocks Microsoft Corp and Intel Corp had a languid day day, smaller issues showed strength, traders said. The Russell 2000 index, a key barometer of small-capitalization stocks, gained 1.40 points or 0.38 percent to 371.46.
Nasdaq shares traded in a moderate ranging, hitting a high of 1378 and dipping to a low of 1367.

"It was a lackluster session. Folks got passed the Fed's decision and now we're heading into a long weekend. People are just going to let things lie until next week," said Nelson Gold, senior vice president of over-the-counter trading at Interstate-Johnson Lane Corp.
Shares of CFM Technologies Inc dropped about 21 percent to 29-1/2 after the company said agressive pricing will hurt gross margins for the rest of the fiscal year.
